era: c.1600: Momoyama into early Edo, Keicho shinto (1596-1615), in a period uchigatana koshirae
how_to_read: Every entry has value (+ unit in the key), source (who says so), ref (ids in refs_index.json or ref_measurements.json). assumed=true marks a value no source gives; reason says why it was picked. The generator (tools/katana_geom.py, models.build_katana, textures.katana_*) reads this file; nothing else sets a katana dimension.

primary_refs.blade_dimensions: tsuruginoya_F00247: katana by Horikawa Kunihiro, c. Keicho 8 (1603), NBTHK Juyo. One coherent, fully measured Keicho blade; the other Keicho blades are cross-checks.
primary_refs.blade_shape_photos: met27600 (Takahiro, dated 1622) and met27601 (Munetsugu, early-mid 17th c.), Met Open Access CC0: silhouette, kissaki, colours are measured from these (ref_measurements.json).
primary_refs.mount_photo: wc_motoshige_koshirae = TNM F-19992, uchigatana koshirae of the late 16th / early 17th c. (ColBase CC BY 4.0): tsuka shape, wrap, same colours.

frame._note: Engine constraints, not research: the grip frame proven against vanilla Sword (medieval_sword.anm IK). Item frame p3d = (dx, dz, -dy). Kept exactly.

guard_base_y_m.source: vanilla Sword guard base, measured by grip_proof.py

edge_axis.source: REPORT.md decision 4: wrists and elbows sit on -Z in the sword IK, so the edge faces +Z (knuckle side)

machi_at_guard_base.reason: the habaki's rear end, the munemachi and the blade-side face of the seppa/tsuba stack coincide to within a few mm on a mounted katana; nagasa is counted from here

omote_face.source: omote = the face seen when the katana is worn edge-up at the left hip; seen tip-up with the edge on the left (the Met kissaki photo view) that is the -X face of this frame (Blender/game view, render_blender.py side camera)

nagasa_cm.measured_as: straight line from the munemachi to the point (ncjsc_measure)

sori_cm.measured_as: deepest gap between the nagasa chord and the mune (ncjsc_measure)

sori_type.source: F00247 'shallow sori'; the deepest point measured on the Met 27600 photo sits at 0.507 of the nagasa from the machi

sori_peak_from_machi_frac.source: met27600 photo: 0.507; modelled as a circular arc, which peaks at exactly 0.5

sakihaba_cm.source: F00247 (width at the yokote); 'little difference between moto and saki width'

taper.value: linear from motohaba at the machi to sakihaba at the yokote
taper.reason: no source gives the width curve; dealers give only the two end widths and the Met photo samples (2.12 / 2.33 / 2.60 / 2.84 cm at 0.1/0.25/0.5/0.75 of the length) are close to linear

funbari.reason: the flare is in the first ~2 cm above the machi, inside the 3.3 cm habaki

motokasane_cm.measured_as: thickness of the mune at the munemachi (glossaria_kasane, ncjsc_measure)

sakikasane_cm.measured_as: thickness of the mune at the yokote

shinogi_thickness_over_kasane.reason: kasane is taken at the mune; the shinogi is the thickest line of a shinogi-zukuri blade and F00247 says the shinogi is 'somewhat high'. No source gives the ratio

shinogi_from_mune_over_width.reason: F00247: 'wide shinogi-ji for the width'. Met photos give 0.39-0.44 (ref_measurements kissaki.shinogi_from_edge_frac 0.564 / 0.607), but those photos see a little of the mune, which widens the dark band; 0.36 = a wide shinogi-ji on a blade seen square-on

mune.source: F00247 shape line (mitsu-mune); Sesko: Keicho-shinto Soshu-den smiths used mitsu-mune

mune_top_over_kasane.reason: flat top of the mitsu-mune; proportion typical of mitsu-mune cross-section diagrams, not measured

mune_bevel_depth_over_kasane.reason: depth of each mune bevel toward the edge; a small facet, as the bright mune line in the Met kissaki photos (about 3-8 % of the width)

niku.unit: extra half-thickness on the hira-ji, fraction of the shinogi half-thickness
niku.source: Sesko: noticeably low niku on Keicho-shinto blades
niku.reason: 'low' is sourced; the 5 % number is not

hi.source: F00247 lists no carving or groove; no hi in the Met 27600 / 27601 photos

size_class.source: F00247 shape line; Sesko: extended chu- or o-kissaki on Keicho shinto

length_over_sakihaba.source: measured on the Met kissaki close-ups: 1.68 (met27600) and 1.81 (met27601); the upper value because F00247 says 'extended'

point_on_mune_line.source: both Met close-ups: the point lies on the mune line (width at the point 0.9-1.5 % of the yokote width)

fukura_profile_t_w.note: t = distance from the point along the blade / kissaki length (0 = point, 1 = yokote); w = width across the blade / sakihaba. The edge sweeps up in a convex curve (fukura) and meets the straight mune at the point.
fukura_profile_t_w.source: average of the two measured Met profiles (ref_measurements.json kissaki[*].fukura_profile_s_w)

yokote.value: straight line across the hira from the edge to the shinogi, square to the mune
yokote.source: Met 27600 / 27601 close-ups (horizontal on the vertical blade)

ko_shinogi_profile_t_d.note: d = the ko-shinogi's distance from the mune / the shinogi's distance from the mune at the yokote. The ko-shinogi runs on from the shinogi at the yokote and curves into the mune at the point.
ko_shinogi_profile_t_d.source: measured from 0.4 to 1.0 on both Met close-ups (ref_measurements kissaki[*].ko_shinogi_s_frac); below t=0.4 the band is too thin to measure and is taken straight to the point

thickness_profile.reason: the kissaki thins to a near-sharp point; no source gives thickness inside the kissaki

thickness_exp.reason: keeps the kissaki full (thick) until near the point, as a fukura that is 'full' implies

style.value: nie-deki, low, shallow notare with ko-gunome and pointed elements, a few small ashi, kinsuji and sunagashi; subdued nioiguchi

height_over_width.reason: F00247 says 'low yakiba' (yakiba hikuku); low = roughly a quarter of the width. Not measured

notare_wavelength_cm.reason: shallow, long undulation; about 8 waves over the nagasa

boshi.value: sugu (runs straight along the fukura), komaru (small round turn), very shallow kaeri, hakikake

boshi_kaeri_over_kissaki.reason: 'very shallow kaeri': the return along the mune is short

kaeri_width_over_boshi.reason: the kaeri is a narrow band along the mune

pointed_every_n_gunome.reason: F00247: pointed (togari) elements 'mixed in', so a minority of the peaks

calm_before_yokote_cm.reason: the waves die out into a straight (sugu) boshi

boshi_appearance.value: hardened band follows the fukura at the hamon height, turns round in a small arc short of the point

hamon.source: median of the hamon band below the yokote, met27600 (200,213,230) and met27601 (207,216,226)

ji.source: median of the hira-ji between hamon and shinogi, met27600 (91,107,126) and met27601 (97,110,126)

shinogi_ji.source: met27600 burnished shinogi-ji (met27601 reflects the black studio and reads 2,4,9, not used)

wrap_leather.source: median of the bright wrap pixels on the TNM F-19992 tsuka

same_lacquered.source: median of the dark window pixels on the TNM F-19992 tsuka

tsuba_iron.source: median of the dark iron ground on Met 30091 (75,70,67), Met 30092 (82,72,70) and TNM F-19992 (72,73,70). A first TNM sample (101,69,67) was tinted by the red saya behind the tsuba and was dropped

shakudo.reason: shakudo patina is blue-black; no measured sample in hand

horn_lacquer.reason: black lacquered horn (nihonto_tensho_juyo); black lacquer value

gold_foil.reason: gold foil on the habaki (aoi_tadayoshi_1615); gold colour value

length_cm.reason: katana habaki are commonly 3-3.5 cm; no measured c.1600 habaki in hand

wall_cm.reason: sheet thickness + gap; reads as a collar

thickness_cm.reason: plain thin washers either side of the tsuba

margin_cm.reason: a seppa is a little bigger than the fuchi outline

tsuba.source: F00247 round iron tsuba; Tensho Juyo koshirae round iron; TNM F-19992 round iron openwork; Met 30091/30092 round

fuchi.source: F00247 fuchi: shakudo nanako with crests and arabesque

flare.reason: angled sides: the tsuba end is ~5 % larger than the wrap end

kashira.material: black lacquered horn, the wrap passes over its top (kashira-kake)

length_cm.reason: Tensho kashira is small, 'about the same size as the fuchi'

length_cm.note: tsuba-side face of the fuchi to the end of the kashira

width_cm.reason: side-to-side width; only one view of a period tsuka is in hand. Oval tsuka are ~0.75-0.8 as wide as they are deep

waist_from_fuchi_frac.reason: waist a little nearer the fuchi, between the hands

kashira_end_scale.reason: Tensho kashira about the size of the fuchi; TNM F-19992 tapers slightly

tsuka_sori_cm.source: Tensho Juyo koshirae tsuka curvature 0.2 cm
tsuka_sori_cm.reason: curve continues the blade's arc (kashira toward the mune)

same.value: black lacquered ray skin (same), seen in the wrap windows
same.source: TNM F-19992 photo (black windows); Tensho koshirae; same was lacquered up to the Momoyama period. F00247 has red lacquered same (not used)

wrap.source: F00247 leather wrap; Tensho Juyo lacquered leather; TNM F-19992 buff tape
wrap.pattern: hineri-maki: two tapes cross on each face centre line, diamond windows of same between the crossings

pitch_cm.source: TNM F-19992: 15 windows on one face, median pitch 1.26 cm

window_half_length_over_pitch.source: TNM F-19992 windows are narrow diamonds about 0.4-0.45 of the pitch long

window_half_height_over_depth.source: TNM F-19992 windows span about 55 % of the tsuka depth

menuki.design: crawling dragon, shakudo with gold uttori
menuki.placement: omote at the 3rd window from the fuchi, ura at the 3rd window from the kashira

window_from_end.source: cottontail_tosogu (omote: 3rd window from the fuchi; ura: 3rd from the kashira)

length_cm.reason: katana menuki are commonly 3-4.5 cm long

count.source: a Keicho blade with one mekugi-ana

below_machi_cm.source: first mekugi-ana on the Met 27600 nakago, 6.42 cm below the machi

build._note: Kept from the original build (REPORT.md): same LOD scheme, same Geometry / Memory / View / Fire LODs, same mass and memory point names.

kissaki_segments.note: yokote to point at detail 1.0, packed toward the point where the fukura bends hardest

habaki_front_chamfer_cm.note: set-back and shrink of the front edge
habaki_front_chamfer_cm.reason: the front edge of a habaki is eased

fuchi_lip_cm.reason: the fuchi stands a little proud of the wrap

kashira_profile.note: [fraction of the kashira length from the wrap end, scale of the tsuka section]
kashira_profile.reason: small rounded horn cap, slightly proud of the wrap, about the fuchi's size

memory_points_kept.source: original build (models.katana_memory); meleerangeend = the point + offset
